prompt.task: Freeze one source-grounded initial-design hypothesis for a new target. Select exactly three candidate IDs before any target outcome is revealed.

archived_failure_lessons: Unconstrained maximin diversity can leave the source-supported quality region and cause negative transfer.
Prefer a quality anchor plus complementary candidates that remain plausible under source evidence.
Do not infer or invent target outcomes. Candidate source scores are priors, not target measurements.

A quality-only design concentrated in one catalyst or condition family can give a good first observation but leave the subsequent target GP poorly conditioned. Preserve source-supported geometric coverage.

required_output_schema.mechanism: why the source evidence should transfer
failure_conditions: conditions that would falsify or limit this skill

constraints: Use exactly three unique candidate IDs from candidate_shortlist unless abstain=true.
Do not request or speculate about hidden target outcomes.
Do not change the target GP-UCB kernel, reveal budget, or candidate pool.
Use source evidence and scientific plausibility, not candidate ID order.

Select one source-quality anchor and two complementary probes. The three candidates must span at least two distinct group values when the shortlist contains multiple groups; selecting all three from one group is invalid.
Complementary probes must remain strongly source-supported while adding coverage across catalyst identity and numeric operating conditions.

parsed_response.hypothesis: In the Morpholine–tBuBrettPhos target, 100 °C conditions using strong non-nucleophilic amidine bases should outperform the 30 °C and triethylamine options, with the most likely high-yield region centered on same-precatalyst-supported MTBD/DBU settings at moderate residence time and ~1.1–2.2 base equivalents.
parsed_response.mechanism: Transfer is grounded primarily in the same-precatalyst datasets, where tBuBrettPhos repeatedly shows its best outcomes under hotter conditions with strong organic bases, and where both short- and longer-residence successful regimes exist. Candidate 005 is the strongest source-supported anchor because it matches the common high-performing pattern for tBuBrettPhos: 100 °C, strong amidine base, moderate residence time, and moderate base equivalents. Candidate 002 tests whether the similarly source-supported DBU family is superior at comparable long residence time and slightly higher equivalents, consistent with excellent aniline+tBuBrettPhos performance. Candidate 010 preserves source-supported geometric coverage by probing the low-equivalent, very short-residence DBU regime that was also successful in aniline+tBuBrettPhos, helping distinguish whether morpholine follows a fast-turnover or longer-contact optimum while remaining inside the credible quality region.
failure_conditions: If morpholine behaves unlike the other amine-class substrates under tBuBrettPhos and instead prefers weaker or more nucleophilic bases, this hypothesis fails.
If the doubled precatalyst loading in the target changes the base-response landscape enough that source-local optima no longer transfer, the selected region may not be best.
If 30 °C candidates or triethylamine candidates outperform these 100 °C amidine-base selections, the central transfer claim is falsified.
If all three selected candidates give similarly poor yields, then same-precatalyst source similarity was not predictive for this target.
